### 2026-10-28: # Devlog 1: Getting started!

**5.3h**

# Devlog 1: Getting started!

-- NOTE TO REVIEWERS --

Hey! Thanks for reviewing my project. Essentially, I missed the deadline without logging, so I'm just speed logging rn. Here's a ss:

![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 22.19.32](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/cea0ed53014969ea2751974ac42d81fc1b5706e480e3c2f3c6689300e81c79cd.png)

-- That's it for y'all, thanks for reviewing! --

Hey! I finished on the Schematic and most of the footprint assignment.

Firstly, I started with the basic Waveshare ESP32-S3-ZERO, but soon found out that using 12 keys needed a lot more spots. I did some research online, and I filtered it down to one section: The Raspberry Pi Pico's. They are

![Screenshot 2026-10-21 at 21.20.10](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/2fe66be52e9c0185895690c2f292a5efd0928a6adca43d412ec9211f427da14a.png)
(God this looks disastrous)

The reason why I have added all of these 1MΩ Resistors is due to the fact that the board is not compatible with these touch thingies, which the Waveshare board has, so I need to manually add them in myself.

Here are some of the other parts that I added:
![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 20.00.06](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/1eb5f5fdffa1f85018f45545f6a13a34b56e4a82785f9aae6a8d42b56ba59a87.png)
(The RGB LEDs!)

![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 20.00.45](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/0b19fbdcfaa5ae20604e038b4d041197879b909ac6cc105dc6d593ed2e4493c9.png)

(The switches!)

![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 20.01.12](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/11df841201aea6e344938bf8f3dcdb8ef438666d404f6ff3f8aff11e268afabc.png)
(Rotary Switch)

![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 20.01.28](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/252800bddb7ff19296470431a02c57c37783106c0a0f06cee077297987cdd2fc.png)
(Sliders!)

![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 20.01.38](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/5220c9538a3656e4e986b72dd8978d57c4eacf6b908db36787f7d05e4e4ded50.png)
The board!!!

I also added in all of the footprints, (except for the touch keys)

![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 20.02.31](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/505fafd4a2157ed3349b376a04a51ea8b300b5437c43716151dad24b87aec049.png)

It took me like a really long time to find the RPi pico schematic, as snapmagic was loading really slowly, and not letting me download the files. After trying for like 20 minutes or so, I just tried using a less detailed model of it, but I think it would work.
Ok, thats it for this devlog. Byeeee!!!

### 2026-10-28: # Devlog 2

**2.7h**

# Devlog 2
Today, I worked on the footprint for my Capacitive Keys. The first Issue that I hit when designing was that my blocks were not perfectly aligned. Basically, the axis align system was messing up the alignment, even after grouping elements.
![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 20.12.55](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/e16730c396c23f97fa8877adba6e79a5d6be152a47efb3572aba7ad3ec31390b.png)

After a long time, I just resorted to watching some youtube videos to try to fix it. I finally found that just tuning the grid snap and axis snap, you can actually get it to look correctly, which I finally got done and applied to my symbol. Heres a comparison:

Old:
![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 20.17.28](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/e5a31c189f054adeb5779968fcbc20bca22838f0d045badad9bacbcbdf921f97.png)

New:
![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 20.34.10](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/dV5DNWN0CEIJqjXEjV5AkLty6hRHMTTp/6233df16ab6e33a899bc65cdf0d1f4ac973e8ebdfd605ff912f9a73e66e5bd27.png)

Ok, thats all for now. Bye!!!
